required_manual_checks.description: The owner's answer to preflight Q1 (ship rank 5 'Strong fit, untouched' even if the section 8 count is near zero; recommended: yes) is recorded in the checkpoint before the rank is built. If the answer is no, rank 5 is omitted and the remaining ranks keep their numbers.

Exactly the six reasons of SLICE-2A3-PREFLIGHT.md section 2, over active, anchored, not-closed prospects, each prospect showing only its highest applicable reason: 1 Overdue follow-up; 2 Due today (America/Los_Angeles); 3 Warm, no next step (latest contact outcome interested, callback_requested or meeting_set, and no open follow-up); 4 Proposal out (stage proposal, no contact in 7+ days); 5 Strong fit, untouched (score tier hot or priority, never contacted); 6 New, assigned to the viewer (never contacted, oldest assignment first). Tie-breaks inside a rank: earliest due, then oldest last contact, then name. Scope follows the existing Mine/Team toggle. Computed in SQL through the existing read path, bounded, with a count per rank; no write, no schema change, no migration, no new index (needing one is a STOP and a scope change).

Rank 5 needs computeScore (core/crm/scoring.ts, unchanged) in SQL. The SQL tier expression must equal computeScore's tier for the ENTIRE input domain: every combination of website_quality (each enum value and NULL), decision_maker_access (true, false, NULL), project_urgency (each value and NULL) and niche_alignment (true, false, NULL), asserted by an exhaustive test that fails if either side changes. Absence is not evidence (D-1): NULL awards nothing on both sides.

On /sales, 'Priority · N' is the first section, bounded to 10 rows, each row stating its reason in words (no hidden number), with 'See all' to /sales/list?priority=1. /sales/list accepts the priority filter alongside the existing filters and orders by rank then the tie-breaks. Existing queue sections, owner controls and partner restrictions are unchanged. Galaxy remains the default landing (Q2b not in scope).

db tests on the fixture: a prospect qualifying for two ranks appears once, under the higher; each rank has a positive and a negative case at its boundary (due today vs overdue at LA midnight, 7-day proposal edge, warm outcomes vs others, assigned-to-viewer vs another member); the partner's Mine scope never shows another member's rows; Team scope for the partner shows only what the partner may already read.

A PostgreSQL 17.6 fixture at production size (at least 3,100 prospects, with contacts, follow-ups and transitions spread across ranks) times every Sales section query including Priority, as owner and as partner; timings and EXPLAIN shape recorded in the checkpoint (value-free). Any section query above 500 ms on the fixture is a finding to resolve or escalate, not to hide.

Slice 1C rendered proof with the fixture-PG17 method (never production): headless-Chrome screenshots at 390x844, 640x900, 667x375, 768x1024, 1024x800 and 1440x900 as owner AND partner; no horizontal overflow; no target under 44px on coarse pointers; 16px form text on phones; keyboard pass (focus order and visible focus through the Priority section and the list filter). Screenshots stay out of the repository; the checkpoint records what was checked.

Diff limited to the write paths; any new test file is classified in gate-2g1.ts in this slice. No production contact by the builder. Deploy happens only after 2A.3a-2 is promoted, through a separate rollout task.

title: 2A.3b Sales priority: six stated reasons as bounded SQL, a 'Priority · N' section on /sales, a priority list filter, reason labels on rows
